errors()

The errors() method registers observational error callbacks on a FeatureCell that execute during the Error stage of the pipeline, after the error has been fully normalized, finalized, and committed to state. Error callbacks provide a controlled extension point for observing Vault error events without influencing error authority, pipeline execution, or state commitment.

Method Contract Summary

  • Error callbacks are registered declaratively on a FeatureCell instance
  • Callbacks execute only after the error state has been finalized
  • Callbacks receive the finalized Vault error and an immutable state snapshot
  • Callbacks must not mutate state or transform errors
  • Callback execution does not affect pipeline control or error resolution

The errors() method defines observation only. It does not normalize, transform, suppress, or recover from errors. Its responsibility is limited to attaching post-finalization observers to the FeatureCell runtime surface.

Note

The errors() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each invocation appends callbacks to the FeatureCell’s error callback list. Callbacks execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, the recommended practice is to register related error callbacks as a single ordered array to preserve clarity and intentional execution ordering.

Example

The errors() method registers one or more error callbacks that observe finalized Vault error events. These callbacks execute after the error has been committed to FeatureCell state and exposed through the global error surface.

Example: Registering Error Callbacks

{{`employeeCell
  .errors([
    (error, state) => {
      console.error('Employee FeatureCell error:', error.message);
      console.info('Last known state:', state.value);
    }
  ])
  .initialize();`}}

What this does

  • Registers one or more error callbacks on the FeatureCell
  • Callbacks execute after error normalization and state commitment
  • Callbacks receive the finalized Vault error and immutable state snapshot
  • No error transformation, recovery, or pipeline control occurs

This demonstrates the intended use of errors() as an observational hook for logging, diagnostics, monitoring, or legacy compatibility handling.
